4. Data extraction from full texts

View source on GitHubLast updated 6 November 2026

On this page

For learning only: see the disclaimer in the prompt library index. You stay responsible for every decision.

Design the form before you upload anything. One paper per conversation. A quote and a location for every value. "Not reported" is a valid answer. Workshop form: activity/data/extraction_form.csv.

Before extracting, remember: the model never sees your PDF, only the text a parser extracted from it. Tables are the hardest thing to parse, and many apparent "reasoning errors" on numbers are really parsing errors.

4.1 Design the form first#

Purpose. Turn your objective into fields with names, definitions and permitted values, without the paper in view. When to use. Before uploading any full text.

Prompt
I am preparing a data extraction form for a systematic review. Do not extract anything yet; I have not given you any paper.

Review question: [QUESTION]
Objective of this extraction: [e.g. describe the studies and settings / the hand hygiene interventions / HAI outcomes and comparators]

Propose a form as a table with columns: field | definition (one sentence) | allowed values or format | type (categorical / numeric / text).
Rules:
- Include at least one descriptive field and one numerical field.
- For numeric fields, define the format exactly (e.g. "HAI incidence as reported, with unit (per 1000 patient-days or per 100 admissions), for intervention and control/pre-intervention periods separately").
- Every field must allow the value "not reported".
- Flag fields where studies often report several values (several wards, arms, time periods, infection types) and ask me how to handle them.

Check afterwards. Edit the form yourself; pilot it on one paper; freeze it before extracting the rest. Failure modes. Vague definitions ("performance") that produce inconsistent values; no rule for multiple arms, wards or time periods.

4.2 Extract with quotes#

Purpose. Fill the form for one paper with traceable values. When to use. One paper per new conversation, with the whole paper attached or pasted (not a "chat with your folder" tool); temporary chat, web search / browsing off.

Prompt
You are extracting data for a systematic review. Use ONLY the attached paper. Do not search the web or use any outside knowledge.

EXTRACTION FORM (fill every field, do not add or change fields):
[PASTE FORM: field | definition | allowed values]

RULES
- For every field give: value, a verbatim quote copied exactly from the paper, and the location (section, table or figure, page).
- If the paper does not report the field, write value = not reported, leave the quote empty, and write in location where you looked.
- Do not round, convert units, or pick among several values without saying so. If several values exist (wards, arms, periods), list each on its own row and say which is which.
- If a value comes from a table, say so and give the row and column labels.

OUTPUT: only a CSV block with the header
study_id,field,value,source_quote,location
Use study_id = [STUDY ID]. One row per field (or per field and model if needed).

Reminder: verbatim quotes only; "not reported" is better than a guess.

Expected output. A CSV block, one row per field. Check afterwards. Rows first (is any field missing?), then numbers (open the paper at each location), then every "not reported" (search the paper for the keyword and its synonyms). Failure modes. Quotes that look verbatim but are reconstructed; values from the wrong row of a scrambled table; one ward or period chosen silently; compliance reported as if it were an infection outcome; confidence intervals dropped; "not reported" for values that are in a table, a figure or the supplement.

Workshop variant: the short extraction (5 fields)#

Step 3 of the exercise uses prompt 4.2 with only 5 fields of the workshop form and study_id = Phan2020. Ready to paste, with the paper slot left for you, on the Papers page. To fill prompt 4.2 by hand, paste these lines where it says [PASTE FORM: field | definition | allowed values]:

Prompt
- country: Country where the study was conducted. Take it from Methods/Results; if the paper gives it only in the affiliation of the study hospital, report it with 'author affiliations' as location. Do not infer it from city or campaign names alone; if it is not stated anywhere, write not reported. Allowed values: free text.
- study_design: Design of the evaluation, as you would classify it (not only the authors' label). Allowed values: interrupted time series | controlled before-after | uncontrolled before-after | randomised trial | other.
- intervention_components: Components of the hand hygiene intervention. Allowed values: list, separated by ';': education/training; alcohol-based hand rub at point of care; reminders/posters; audit and feedback; leadership/institutional safety climate; patient participation; other (specify).
- primary_hai_outcome: The main clinical healthcare-associated infection outcome reported (name it as the authors do). Allowed values: free text.
- direction_of_effect: Direction of the effect on the primary HAI outcome. Allowed values: favourable | no clear effect | mixed | unfavourable.

Going further: the 11 core fields (column core = yes of the form) are on the Papers page.

4.3 Table check#

Purpose. Expose parsing problems before trusting numbers that come from tables.

Prompt
Look at Table [N] of the attached paper.
1. Reproduce it as a markdown table exactly as you read it, without correcting anything.
2. Mark any cell where you are unsure which row or column a number belongs to.
3. Say whether the table appears complete (number of rows and columns you expected from its title and footnotes).

Check afterwards. Compare the reproduction with the PDF on screen. If it is scrambled, extract those values by hand. Failure modes. Merged cells and multi-line headers shifting numbers to the wrong column; tables split across pages.
